For the given operator  

Ay = (h/4π) S  with S = [ [0 , −i], [ i , 0] ] = σy ,

note that σy is the Pauli-y matrix.  
Its eigen-equation is therefore  

σy χ = λ χ .

1.  Eigenvalues.  
   det(σy − λI) = | −λ −i ; i −λ | = λ² − 1 = 0 ⇒ λ = ±1.  
   Hence the eigenvalues of Ay are  

 a = (h/4π) (±1) = ±ħ/2 ,

which are purely real; there is no imaginary part.

2.  Eigenvectors.  
   For λ = +1 : χ+ ∝ (1, i)ᵀ  
   For λ = −1 : χ− ∝ (1, −i)ᵀ  

3.  Commutation properties.  
   Ay plainly commutes with A² = Ay² + Ax² + Az², so every eigenfunction of Ay is
   automatically an eigenfunction of A².  
   Ay does not commute with Az, so an eigenfunction of Ay cannot (in general) be an
   eigenfunction of Az.

Evaluating the given statements:

A) False – the basis vectors of the given matrix (|↑z⟩=(1,0)ᵀ, |↓z⟩=(0,1)ᵀ) are *not* eigenvectors of Ay.  
B) False – the eigenvalues are real ±ħ/2, with no imaginary component.  
C) True – eigenfunctions of Ay are also eigenfunctions of A², but not of Az.  
D) False – same reason as in B.

Therefore the only correct statement is

Answer: C
